pdf_file_read: ROS (Buda) - A Systematic Study of the Class Imbalance Problem in Convolutional Neural Networks (Neural Networks 2018).pdf (+ Supplementary 1 Appendix A Reshuffled Splits, plots only)

datasets.name: MNIST
datasets.source_repo: other: MNIST benchmark (LeCun, Bottou, Bengio, & Haffner, 1998)
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Each class uniformly at random subsampled to no more than 5000 training examples (balanced subset: 5000 train / 1000 test per class, Table 1; image 28x28x1), then artificially imbalanced (step and linear imbalance); minority classes randomized, 50 repetitions per setting; test set left balanced (Sec. 3.3.1, 3.4, p.4-5)

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Original 5000 train / 1000 test per class (32x32x3); training set artificially imbalanced (step and linear); minority classes = lowest label values; test set left balanced (Sec. 3.3.2, p.4-5)

datasets.name: ILSVRC-2012
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Majority classes reduced from 1200 to 1000 examples (1000 train / 50 test per class in balanced subset, Table 1; images rescaled, smaller side 256); classes with <1000 cases always chosen as minority; three step-imbalanced subsets, highest imbalance run 3 times with randomized minority classes (Sec. 3.3.3, p.5)
datasets.ref: Table 1, p.4 (printed 252); Sec. 3.3.3 p.5; Table 4 p.8 (printed 256)

ir_definition: ρ = max_i{|C_i|} / min_i{|C_i|} (ratio between number of examples in majority and minority classes, Eq. 2); step imbalance also uses µ = fraction of minority classes (Eq. 1); linear imbalance uses same ρ with linear interpolation of class sizes

outcome.smote_name_as_printed: SMOTE (mentioned only in Sec. 2.1/2.2 literature review, p.2; not evaluated)
baselines_all: Two-phase training with pre-training on randomly oversampled dataset
Two-phase training with pre-training on randomly undersampled dataset

chosen.condition: ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012) step imbalance; all three settings (µ = 0.1, ρ = 10; µ = 0.8, ρ = 50; µ = 0.9, ρ = 100 with three runs)

win_claim.quote: the method of addressing class imbalance that emerged as dominant in almost all analyzed scenarios was oversampling

uncertain: Run labels '(run 1/2/3)' for the three µ = 0.9, ρ = 100 columns are added by extractor; Table 4 prints three unlabeled columns under one header (p.8)
Classifier choice: no classifier highlighted in abstract; first reported is LeNet-5 (MNIST) but MNIST/CIFAR-10 results are plots only, so ResNet-10 (only numeric table) used (p.4, p.8)
n_instances left null: Table 1 gives per-class balanced counts only (5000/1000, 5000/1000, 1000/50), totals for imbalanced subsets vary by setting and are not printed (p.4)
Only Baseline, Oversampling, Undersampling were run on ImageNet; best_other is chosen from these two (p.5, p.8)
notes: Comparative study, not a new method: proposed = random minority oversampling ('Oversampling'). SMOTE not evaluated. All three datasets are 10- or 1000-class multiclass with artificially induced step/linear imbalance on the training set; test sets kept balanced. MNIST and CIFAR-10 results (Figs. 3-7) are plots only. Table 4 Undersampling values: 96.85, 94.98, 88.35, 84.08, 83.74. Supplementary Appendix A (CIFAR-10 reshuffled splits) contains plots only; Appendix B (convergence plots) and Appendix C (confusion matrices) not used for numeric comparison. Main comparator: Baseline (do-nothing).
